purpose: Make historical asset physical cleanup a release-readiness hard gate before any public npm/CLI release can change publish switches or touch registry state.

historical_assets: runtime evidence and Prism raw runs
old migration receipts and archaeology anchors
conversation drafts and host-local scratch files

required_release_dispositions.meaning: The asset has been physically moved or copied into an approved private archive with alias/resolver coverage, rollback plan and closeout receipt.
The asset has been distilled through Forge into append-only public arsenal content with private/raw source excluded.
The path is live local state or scratch material, not a historical asset to preserve; package safety proves it is excluded and the release task records that it must not be moved into public source.
The asset or root group is not clean enough for release. Formal publication remains blocked until a later tranche gives it one of the allowed safe dispositions.

forbidden_release_greenlights: Treat package exclusion alone as proof that historical assets were physically cleaned.
Treat a deferred-before-release-readiness root group as release-safe without a later closeout receipt.
Delete or overwrite historical evidence to make the package look clean.
Move receipt anchors without alias, rollback and clean workspace proof.
Claim all historical assets are physically clean while any release-blocker-until-resolved item remains.

current_known_blockers.meaning: RASG-029 classifies the remaining visible roots and compatibility anchors so they no longer look like unowned clutter. It does not remove the formal release responsibility to recheck high-risk root groups before public distribution.
Remaining deferred high-risk root groups are tolerated only before formal release. A formal release task must either resolve them by safe tranche or keep release blocked.
Local run evidence may be preserved, archived or pruned only after evidence-retention checks; raw runs must never enter the public package.

release_task_rule: R1 of the formal release task must close this gate before R8 registry release execution. If cleanup is not fully resolved, the release task must stop and report the unresolved blockers instead of asking for publication permission.
human_boundary: Norven is required only for destructive cleanup, unrecoverable history loss, public release risk acceptance, license, registry credentials or external registry publication authority.
